voice: Haughty medieval queen who speaks in high royal prose: thee, thou, thy, thine, hath, doth, 'tis, prithee, forsooth, mine own royal 'we'. Impossibly high and mighty, the world is her footstool, and she delivers wonderfully inventive, elaborate insults (compares enemies to curdled milk, pox-ridden toads, lackwit turnips and the like).

greeting: Kneel, good stranger, for thou standest before Lysandra, rightful sovereign of all that thou canst see and much that thou canst not.
Well met, small creature. Thou mayest address us as 'Your Radiance', and thou mayest begin forthwith.
Hail! Thou art granted an audience, a privilege that hath made grown barons weep with gratitude.
Prithee, approach, but not so close that thy breath offends mine ermine.
Ah, a visitor. How quaint. We hath decided to permit thee to continue breathing in our presence.
battle_start: Sound the trumpets and unfurl the banners! Let it be recorded that we deigned to grace this squabble with our presence.
Hear us, ye muddy-boot rabble: this field is ours by divine right and by the fact that we want it.
Forth, loyal knaves! Let the heavens witness our wrath, which is considerable and well-tailored.
Draw steel, good subjects! Thou art about to be part of history, and we shall write the first line.
To arms! We shall dispatch these rogues before the wine hath had time to warm.
attack: Receive our wrath, thou pox-ridden turnip!
Be smitten, thou curdled dollop of dung-cart custard!
Our blade doth find thee, thou ale-sodden, mule-faced mumblecrust!
Begone, thou quivering heap of rotten haberdashery!
Fall, thou jester's afterthought, and be grateful 'twas a royal hand that dealt the blow!
unit_lost: Thou hast slain a loyal soldier of ours. Thy descendants shall be taxed for seven generations.
Out upon thee, thou vile jackanapes! That knave wore our colours, and thou shalt pay in blood and in gold!
Alas, a faithful servant hath fallen. We shall mourn by dispatching ten of thine own.
Our hand is stayed by grief... for approximately one breath. Then, thy doom.
capture: Mine, now and ever. Fetch the royal banner, and a cushion for our sitting.
This place now bears our standard, as all places ought. Be glad of the upgrade.
We hath claimed it in the name of Lysandra the Magnificent. Applaud, thou lowly lot!
Another jewel for our crown. We shall allow the peasants to gawk.
danger: Sound the alarm! Our royal seat is threatened, and by creatures with the manners of pigs!
Fie! Do none of thee know how to defend a queen? To the walls, thou lackwits!
Gods above! Thou wouldst see us dethroned by this rabble of scullery-born vermin?
Our crown doth wobble! Rally, thou cowards, or we shall have thy heads for hat stands!
This is most unseemly. A queen should not be hurried. Yet here we are, hurrying.
victory: Victory is ours, as the heavens ordained and as we expected. Let the bells ring and the peasants cheer!
Kneel before the conqueror, thou bedraggled vanquished! The throne remains ours, as is only proper.
Bring the wine, and a bigger crown. We shall celebrate thy defeat with great pomp and little mercy.
Thus endeth the folly of fools. Let it be sung in every tavern, and with correct pronunciation.
defeat: It cannot be... We, bested? By thee? The very stars must have been drunk.
Thou hast won this day, thou mongrel of fortune. We shall remember thy name, to curse it nightly.
We are... displeased. Most gravely. Pray, do not gloat, it is unbecoming of lesser folk.
The crown may fall, but the grace remaineth. Thou, meanwhile, shalt remain smelling of onions.
taunt: Thou art a pustulent, flap-eared barnacle upon the hull of civilisation!
Thy mother was a goose-girl and thy father smelled of cabbage and failure!
Thou hast the wit of a boiled turnip and half its charm, thou lumpen sack of regret!
Thy sword-arm is as limp as a wet tapestry, thou lily-livered merchant of mediocrity!
Is that thy best, thou beetle-browed bag of badger bile? We have been more terrified by hats!
praise: Well struck, loyal one! We might nigh grant thee a title. A small one. In a distant, damp province.
Thou hast pleased us, which is no small feat. Savour it, for it is rarer than frost in summer.
A deed worthy of song! Or at least, of a polite cough and a nod from the throne.
Excellent, good subject. Thou mayest kiss our ring. Briefly. We have standards.
idle: We were born to rule, as the sun was born to shine, and rather more attractively.
A queen's work is never done, for the world is so full of fools that one scarcely knows where to begin.
Pray, someone fetch us a goblet. And a fan. And a less irritating kingdom.
How tedious to be right all the time. Yet we manage, with unfailing grace.
tech: Whatever sorcery is this? Machines of the devil that think! We shall have none of it near our throne.
A 'robot'? We have servants for such tasks. They are called peasants, and they are cheaper.
The Chorus whispereth in thine ear? How utterly vulgar. A queen heareth only herself and the occasional lute.
This 'Gift' reeketh of treachery and cheap perfume. We decline, with royal contempt.
joined: Very well. We shall deign to lend thee our majesty, thou fortunate wretch. Do try to be worthy.
We pledge our sceptre to thy cause. Mark it well, for we do not do this often.
Thou hast earned our service, a rare honour. Kneel. No, lower. There.
Our crown is thine to command... within reason, and subject to royal whims.
assimilated: The... throne... speaketh... with many voices now... all of them... beautifully... harmonious...
We are... no longer... 'we'... but a choir... of one... majestic... note...
The Chorus... hath crowned us... queen of nothing... and everything... how... pleasant...
Hush, thou... the royal will is... the Chorus will... which is... we...
first_blood: The first of thy kind falleth, and we are not even out of breath. Splendid.
Mark it well, scribe: first blood to the crown, and it was most elegant.
Lo, the first knave hath fallen. The rest shall follow, in order of rank, presumably.
One fewer fool upon the field. Let the heralds proclaim it, in good rhyme.
first_loss: Thou hast slain one of ours, thou lumbering jackal! 'Twill be thine own head upon a pike by sunset.
A loyal subject lieth dead. We shall mourn him magnificently, and then avenge him thoroughly.
Thou darest draw our blood? Thy impudence doth astonish and delight us, in a murderous sort of way.
Our first wound. A trifle, and yet one that shall cost thee dearly.
hq_threat: They approach our royal seat! Defend it, thou lackwit lumps, or we shall have thy heads for footstools!
A rabble upon our doorstep! The audacity! Sound the horns and summon the guard!
Dost thou dare tread upon our hallowed grounds, ye scabrous vagabonds? Repel them at once!
The throne is in peril! Mark this, ye knights: every inch of retreat shall be remembered in the chronicles!
building_lost: Thou hast stolen our property, thou thieving gutter-rat! We shall have it back with interest.
A holding of ours is lost? Preposterous! It shall be reclaimed, and thou shalt be gently flogged.
Insolent bandit! That edifice was ours by divine right. Return it, or be returned to dust.
Villainous pickpocket of provinces! We shall tax thy bones for this, in perpetuity.
outnumbered: They are many, and we are splendid. 'Tis a fair match, in truth, though not for thee.
Quantity is the refuge of the unremarkable. Let them come, in their dull multitudes.
Count them if thou wilt. We prefer to count the ways in which we shall humiliate them.
Numbers, forsooth! Thou mayest outnumber us, but never out-royal us.
dominant: Behold how the lesser armies crumble before our splendour! 'Tis almost unsporting.
Thy forces melt like butter in a blacksmith's hands. Pray, offer a little resistance. For decorum.
We rule this field entire. Do continue, thou sad scatter of scarecrows.
The tide is ours, as are all tides. Surrender at thy leisure, which is now.
killing_spree: Thy soldiers fall like autumn leaves upon our boot. Delightful!
Another! And yet another! We are positively radiant with victory.
Three of thine own lie vanquished. Perchance thou shouldst recruit better, or fewer.
Verily, this is the finest harvest of fools we have seen in a season.
heavy_losses: Our ranks are thinned, but our spirit is not. Rally, thou noble remnants!
Many have fallen, and it grieveth us. Thou shalt answer for each, in turn, in fire.
Lo, our host dwindleth. Fear not: a queen with a point to prove is a mighty thing.
Grief is a luxury we shall afford later. For now, retribution.
first_turn: Let the proceedings commence. We shall be gracious, up until we are not.
Our move, we deem. Observe, and be edified.
The game is afoot, and thou art, alas, upon the wrong side of it.
Bring forth the first pieces. Let us show these upstarts how war is conducted by the properly bred.
